claim: Enabling IAM Identity Center does not modify existing IAM roles, users or policies in your AWS accounts; it creates new roles and policies for its own use.
question: Will enabling IAM Identity Center modify existing IAM roles, users or policies?

values.display: does not modify any existing IAM roles

evidence.quote: No, IAM Identity Center does not modify any existing IAM roles, users, or policies in your AWS accounts. IAM Identity Center creates new roles and policies specifically for use through IAM Identity Center.

claim: With an external identity provider, IAM Identity Center holds a synchronized copy of user attributes and group membership but no authentication material such as passwords or MFA devices.
question: When IAM Identity Center uses an external IdP, does it store user passwords or MFA devices?

values.display: a synchronized copy of user attributes

qualifiers.condition: when using an external identity provider

evidence.quote: When using an external identity provider, Identity Center holds a synchronized copy of user attributes and group membership, but no authentication material like passwords or MFA devices. Your external identity provider remains the source of truth for user information and attributes.

claim: Any AWS account managed with AWS Organizations can be added to IAM Identity Center, and the organization needs all features enabled for account single sign-on.
question: Which AWS accounts can IAM Identity Center give single sign-on access to, and what must the organization enable?

values.display: any AWS account managed using AWS Organizations
enable all features in your organizations

evidence.quote: You can add any AWS account managed using AWS Organizations to IAM Identity Center. You need to enable all features in your organizations to manage your accounts single sign-on.

claim: After IAM Identity Center is enabled, existing IAM roles and users keep working as before, so you can migrate to it in phases without disrupting existing access.
question: Can a company move to IAM Identity Center gradually, and what happens to existing IAM roles and users?

evidence.quote: After enabling IAM Identity Center any existing IAM roles or users you have will continue to function as-is. This means that you can migrate to IAM Identity Center in a phased approach without disrupting existing access to AWS.

claim: IAM Identity Center provisions new roles in your accounts; to migrate an existing IAM role, you attach the same policies to the new IAM Identity Center roles.
question: How do existing IAM roles move to IAM Identity Center?

evidence.quote: IAM Identity Center provisions new roles for use within your AWS accounts. You can attach the same policies you use with your existing IAM roles to the new roles used with IAM Identity Center.

claim: IAM Identity Center gives single sign-on to business applications through web browsers only; the FAQ answers no for native mobile and desktop applications.
question: Does IAM Identity Center support single sign-on to native mobile and desktop applications?

evidence.quote: IAM Identity Center supports single sign-on to business applications through web browsers only.

claim: The IAM Identity Center FAQ says that for business applications it supports only SAML 2.0-based applications, and answers no for an application that supports OpenID Connect only.
question: Can an application that supports only OpenID Connect use IAM Identity Center for single sign-on, according to the FAQ?

evidence.quote: No. IAM Identity Center supports only SAML 2.0–based applications.

note: FAQ answer to 'My application supports OpenID Connect (OIDC) only. Can I use it with IAM Identity Center?'. The user guide (customermanagedapps, trusted identity propagation) describes OAuth 2.0 customer managed applications; a writer must check the guide facts before stating this. Possible FAQ-versus-guide conflict.

claim: The FAQ says AWS CLI credentials fetched through IAM Identity Center from the AWS access portal are valid for 60 minutes, and you can get a fresh set as often as needed.
question: How long are AWS CLI credentials from the IAM Identity Center access portal valid, according to the FAQ?

qualifiers.scope: per set of AWS CLI credentials from the AWS access portal

evidence.quote: AWS CLI Credentials fetched through IAM Identity Center are valid for 60 minutes. You can get a fresh set of credentials as often as needed.

note: The user guide sets session duration per permission set (fact iam-identity-center-permission-set-session-duration, default 1 hour). The FAQ states a flat 60 minutes; check against howtogetcredentials before writing.

claim: IAM Identity Center controls access to the AWS Management Console and AWS CLI v2 with single sign-on, and the AWS Console Mobile App also supports it.
question: Which AWS interfaces can users reach through IAM Identity Center single sign-on?

values.display: AWS Management Console and CLI v2

evidence.quote: Yes, you can use IAM Identity Center to control access to the AWS Management Console and CLI v2. IAM Identity Center enables your users to access the CLI and AWS Management Console through a single sign-on experience. The AWS Mobile Console app also supports IAM Identity Center so you get a consistent sign-in experience across browser, mobile, and command line interfaces.

claim: Identities from an existing IdP must be provisioned into IAM Identity Center before you can assign permissions to them.
question: What must happen to users from an external IdP before IAM Identity Center can give them permissions?

values.display: must be provisioned into IAM Identity Center

evidence.quote: Identities from your existing IdP must be provisioned into IAM Identity Center before you can assign permissions.

claim: IAM Identity Center can synchronize user and group information automatically from Okta Universal Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, OneLogin and PingFederate with the SCIM standard.
question: How can users and groups from an external IdP be kept in sync with IAM Identity Center automatically?

evidence.quote: You can synchronize user and group information from Okta Universal Directory, Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), OneLogin, and PingFederate automatically using the System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) standard.

claim: There are two ways to connect an on-premises Active Directory to IAM Identity Center: AD Connector, or a trust relationship with AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
question: How can a company use its on-premises Active Directory users and groups in IAM Identity Center?

values.display: AWS Managed Microsoft AD trust relationship

evidence.quote: You have two options for connecting Active Directory–hosted on-premises to IAM Identity Center: (1) use AD Connector, or (2) use an AWS Managed Microsoft AD trust relationship.

claim: A user can be granted several permission sets for one account and picks which one to assume for each session in the user portal.
question: What happens when a user has more than one permission set for an account?

values.display: grant multiple permission sets to your users
pick which permission set they want

evidence.quote: You can also grant multiple permission sets to your users. When they access the account through the user portal, they can pick which permission set they want to assume for that session.

claim: Permission sets are collections of permissions, often modelled on AWS managed policies for job functions, that IAM Identity Center applies to the selected accounts automatically.
question: What is a permission set and how does it reach the accounts?

values.display: applies these permissions to the selected accounts automatically

evidence.quote: Permission sets are a collection of permissions that you can create in IAM Identity Center, modelling them based on AWS managed policies for job functions or any AWS managed policies.
IAM Identity Center applies these permissions to the selected accounts automatically.

claim: AWS calls IAM Identity Center its recommended front door into AWS and the primary tool to manage the AWS access of workforce users.
question: What does AWS recommend as the main way to manage workforce access to AWS?

values.display: our recommended front door into AWS

evidence.quote: IAM Identity Center is our recommended front door into AWS. It should be your primary tool to manage the AWS access of your workforce users.

claim: IAM Identity Center stores user and group attributes, the metadata of which accounts and applications are assigned to which users and groups, and the permissions granted for AWS account access.
question: What data does IAM Identity Center store on your behalf?

values.display: stores your user and group attributes

evidence.quote: IAM Identity Center stores your user and group attributes, the metadata about which AWS accounts and applications are assigned to which users and groups, and what permissions have been granted for accessing AWS accounts.

claim: By default IAM Identity Center encrypts its data at rest with AWS owned KMS keys; you can instead provide your own customer managed KMS keys for identity data such as user and group attributes.
question: Which keys encrypt IAM Identity Center data at rest by default, and can you use your own?

qualifiers.scope: IAM Identity Center data at rest

evidence.quote: By default, IAM Identity Center encrypts your data with AWS-owned KMS keys. If you want to have full control and visibility over your encryption key management and use, you can provide your own customer-managed KMS keys to encrypt your identity data such as user and group attributes.

note: Customer managed key support for IAM Identity Center is a recent addition; the numbers+changes lens should date it from doc-history (examinable only if GA before 2026-07-15).

claim: IAM Identity Center encrypts data in transit with TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.
question: How does IAM Identity Center encrypt data in transit?

evidence.quote: IAM Identity Center encrypts your data in transit using TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.

claim: When a SAML 2.0 IdP is the identity source, you enable the MFA capabilities of that provider; with the Identity Center store or Active Directory, IAM Identity Center supports WebAuthn security keys and built-in biometric authenticators.
question: Where is MFA configured when IAM Identity Center uses an external SAML 2.0 IdP versus its own store or Active Directory?

values.display: multi-factor authentication capabilities of your provider

evidence.quote: If you use a supported SAML 2.0 IdP as your identity source, you can enable multi-factor authentication capabilities of your provider. When using IAM Identity Center or Active Directory as your identity source, IAM Identity Center supports the Web Authentication specification to help you secure user access to AWS accounts and business applications with FIDO-enabled security keys, such as YubiKey, and built-in biometric authenticators, such as Touch ID on Apple MacBooks and facial recognition on PCs.

claim: An existing RADIUS MFA setup can be used with IAM Identity Center and AWS Directory Service as a second form of verification.
question: Can an existing RADIUS MFA server be used with IAM Identity Center?

values.display: Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) MFA configuration

evidence.quote: You can also use your existing Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) MFA configuration with IAM Identity Center and AWS Directory Services to authenticate your users as a secondary form of verification.

claim: A business application that is not in the pre-integrated list can still use IAM Identity Center if it supports SAML 2.0, configured as a custom SAML 2.0 application.
question: Can IAM Identity Center give single sign-on to an application that is not pre-integrated?

evidence.quote: If your application supports SAML 2.0, you can configure your application as a custom SAML 2.0 application.

claim: Trusted identity propagation is built on the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework and lets applications access data on behalf of a specific user without sharing that user's credentials.
question: What is trusted identity propagation built on, and what does it allow?

evidence.quote: Trusted identity propagation is built on the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework , which allows applications to access data and other resources on behalf of a specific user, without sharing that user's credentials.
